extraction_text: Bhishma narrates an ancient historical dialogue between Brihaspati and Indra to Yudhishthira.
Indra asks Brihaspati how one can correctly act to gain respect and honor from all beings.
Brihaspati advises that proper appeasement brings respect and honor, and that sweet speech can control the world even without material gifts.
Bhishma concludes that Indra followed Brihaspati's advice and urges Yudhishthira to do the same.
Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how a king can protect subjects to gain eternal fame related to dharma.
Bhishma responds that a pure king who protects subjects with a pure heart gains dharma, fame, and benefits in this life and the next.
Yudhishthira questions how one person can possess all the previously mentioned qualities and asks about suitable ministers.
Bhishma advises appointing eight ministers: four Brahmanas, three Shudras, and one Suta, all with specific qualifications like age, wisdom, and purity.
Bhishma warns against secretly hindering state policy, as failure leads to adharma tormenting both king and people, causing them to flee and the kingdom to collapse.
The text describes the duties and principles of a king regarding justice, protection, punishment, and governance.
King Yudhishthira asks his grandfather Bhishma what kind of city a king should live in and whether he should choose an existing one or have one built.
Bhishma acknowledges Yudhishthira's question as appropriate and states he will explain matters related to fortresses/cities.
The king should build six types of forts and reside in a fortified city.
